intro: You are about to step into Antalya Museum, in Antalya province, founded in 1922. It is one of Anatolia's largest museums, home to the imperial and divine sculpture of Perge, Lycian sarcophagi and the Elmalı coin hoard.
history: The museum was founded in 1922, and it began with one person: a schoolteacher whose personal effort aimed to stop the city's antiquities leaving the country. Today the backbone of the collection is Perge. The imperial and divine statues from its theatre and baths form one of the best-preserved groups of Roman sculpture anywhere.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Gallery of Gods and the Gallery of Emperors, then look for the Sarcophagus of Heracles, the Elmalı coin hoard and the Lycian sarcophagi.
facts: Did you know? The upper half of the museum's Weary Heracles was smuggled out in the 1960s and sold in Boston, while the lower half stayed in Antalya. The two halves were finally reunited in 2011. And the museum itself owes its existence to a schoolteacher: it was founded in 1922 through the personal effort of someone trying to keep the city's antiquities from leaving the country.
outro: Our visit to Antalya Museum ends here. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These pieces have survived for centuries; let them keep their story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
